caption: Does “the life is in the blood” predict Jesus? It gives Christians a meaningful framework, but Leviticus states a broad ritual principle—not a unique forecast.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Does blood as life predict Jesus? Leviticus says life is in the blood. Jesus later speaks of giving his life and pouring out his blood for many.
slides.body: Leviticus says life is in the blood. Jesus later speaks of giving his life and pouring out his blood for many.
slides.heading: Does blood as life predict Jesus?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Lev 17:11: For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you to make atonement.
slides.body: For the life of the flesh is in the blood, and I have given it to you to make atonement.
slides.heading: Lev 17:11

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Matt 26:28, BSB: This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
slides.body: This is My blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Matt 26:28

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Why the connection makes sense Leviticus joins blood, life and atonement. Those ideas give Christians a natural framework for understanding Jesus’s death.
slides.body: Leviticus joins blood, life and atonement. Those ideas give Christians a natural framework for understanding Jesus’s death.
slides.heading: Why the connection makes sense

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But it identifies nobody Leviticus explains an altar rule and a ban on eating blood. It does not name a future person. Jesus’s words also echo other Bible passages.
slides.body: Leviticus explains an altar rule and a ban on eating blood. It does not name a future person. Jesus’s words also echo other Bible passages.
slides.heading: But it identifies nobody

title: The life is in the blood
